summary: Build a tiny calculator for binary expressions like '6 * 7': a parser that turns text into an AST, and an evaluator that computes it.
rationale: Parsing and evaluation meet only at the AST shape { op, a, b }, so they can be built and tested independently by different solvers and merged at the root.

nodes.goal: evaluate(parse(text)) computes integer binary expressions with + - * /, and errors propagate correctly.
Parse 'a op b' (integers, optional surrounding/inner whitespace, op in + - * /) into an AST; reject anything else.

exposes: src/parser/index.mjs: export function parse(text: string): { op: '+' | '-' | '*' | '/', a: number, b: number }  // throws SyntaxError on invalid input

nodes.goal: Evaluate an AST node; division by zero is an error, unknown operators are an error.

exposes: src/eval/index.mjs: export function evaluate(ast: { op: string, a: number, b: number }): number  // throws RangeError on division by zero, TypeError on unknown op
